title: Minimal polynomials descend to an integrally closed domain
statement: Let $R\subseteq S$ be an inclusion of commutative integral domains, and let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}(S)$, with their induced field extension $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Here the fraction field consists of quotients $a/b$ with nonzero denominator. Assume $R$ is integrally closed in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $s\in S$ be integral over $R$, meaning that a monic polynomial in $R[T]$ annihilates $s$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Then there is a monic polynomial $Q(T)\in R[T]$ such that $Q(s)=0$ in $S$ and the coefficientwise image of $Q$ in $K[T]$ is the minimal polynomial of $s\in L$ over $K$ (the monic polynomial of least degree annihilating $s$). No module-finiteness, Noetherian or separability assumption is made.

mathlib_match.how: Take Q = minpoly R s. minpoly.isIntegrallyClosed_eq_field_fractions (Mathlib/FieldTheory/Minpoly/IsIntegrallyClosed.lean:47-48) with K=Frac(R), L=Frac(S) gives precisely the coefficientwise equality; both scalar towers are the canonical inclusions into Frac(S). minpoly.monic (Mathlib/FieldTheory/Minpoly/Basic.lean:54) and minpoly.aeval (Basic.lean:89) give the other two clauses. These are direct applications, one per clause; no normality of S or finiteness is needed.
